label: early original-phase step (t=1-4) inputting n/y/u/r/g/s after a t/g/0/2 earlier in the prefix
explanation: Almost only fires in the original phase (98% of mass), at steps 1-4, and mostly at t=2-3 (87% of mass). It never fires at t=0 or on the delimiter, and only rarely in the copy phase. Which token is input matters: n is strongest (6.4x lift), then y, u, r, g, s. Earlier tokens add to this: a t, g, y, 2 or 0 earlier in the prefix (t is strongest) raises both rate and magnitude. The top activations are sequences like t t n, t g n, t t u, 0 t 2 n. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of the input token. It behaves like a soft additive mix of the current token, earlier tokens and position, not a sharp rule. That is why a boolean predicate tops out near F1 0.4-0.45: many steps that match it stay below threshold, and many weaker activations come on other tokens (a, w, i, k, d) at the same positions.
